sections.text: The four divisions of society (the wise, the soldier, the merchant, the labourer) were created by Me, according to the natural distribution of Qualities and instincts. I am the author of them, though I Myself do no action, and am changeless.
न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा।
My actions do not fetter Me, nor do I desire anything that they can bring. He who thus realises Me is not enslaved by action.
एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः।
In the light of wisdom, our ancestors, who sought deliverance, performed their acts. Act thou also, as did our fathers of old.

What is my purpose and destiny? We had been discussing chapter four, Jnana Karma Sannyasa Yoga, Yoga of Renunciation of actions in Knowledge. This is all about knowledge, all about what the real I is. So far in chapters two and three, Bhagavan has been saying that what I consider to be I is not the real I, but that which is permanent, that which is Ajaha (unborn), that which is immortal -- that is me.
Chapter three talked about Karma Yoga: how do I act in this world and not get bound by those actions? Chapter four continues that same theme: how do I act in this world but not get bound by my actions? So the first thing Bhagavan says, Ajaha PI, I am unborn. He clarifies first that lets keep in mind that whats the theme of our discussion? Our theme of our discussion is from chapter two onward is I am unborn. Avya Yatma Immutable.
There is no change ever takes place in the self. The supreme self which is all pervading. In the early part of Vedic literature there was a great emphasis on immortality.
No death, deathlessness. He said that in the later part of this Vedic literature they switched on to Aja. Unbornness, birthlessness.
So all of our stories about the Devas are looking for nectar Amrit. There is always a fear of death. Over a period of time they realized its not the death you should be worried about, it is the birth you should be worried about.
As long as there is birth, there will be death. Only way you can overcome death is by not having birth. Thats where it all started, because of my birth that I am now afraid of death.
If I achieve the birthlessness, deathlessness I already achieved. So therefore Bhagavan clarifies very first declaration in this chapter is Ajaha Apisan, I am unborn. No mutation ever takes place in myself.
Now obviously Bhagavan is speaking from the highest perspective of the all pervading self. But we have also seen that our own self is no different than his self. This room space is no different than the space outside.
Before this building was built, this space was nothing but the continuation of the space outside. I created this conditioning called walls, floor and ceiling. Now this same space is part of the universal space, but I consider it to be a separate room space.
So all the qualities of the space outside still remain intact in the room space. But in my perception, theyre conditioned by the walls, floor and ceiling. In my own existence, it is something similar.
The self which is all pervading in my own self are exactly same. The qualities attributed to the Supreme Self are also valid for my own self. So the first thing is Ajahapi son.
I am unborn as the Supreme Self. Therefore my own self is also unborn. No mutation ever took place.
Space never get contaminated by or affected by bad designs. We design buildings, not all of them are good. So we jokingly say the doctors bury their mistakes.
What do we architects do? We put it out there for the world to see every time we pass it. Who the heck designed this thing? But the space in a good building or a bad building are not affected by an architects design. It remains immutable, imperishable.
This place was not brought from Hanover County. It will never be transported back to Hanover County. So he said, I am unborn.
Therefore you are unborn. No mutation ever took place. But Bhutanam Isvaropi son.
But I am still the Lord of all the beings. Beings are beings because of my presence. And they are created out of my Maya.
It is my Maya which created this universe out of my own self. There was no other material available to Bhagavan when he created this universe other than his own self. But if you say there are other material existing, he is limited.
He is no more unlimited. So if he is unlimited, you have to accept that there was no other material ever available to him to create this universe. And therefore the material he used to create this universe is nothing but his own self.
That self, he says, is immutable. No change ever took place in it. Only in your perception.
Out of your ignorance. Out of my ignorance, I create my world and identify with this body, mind and intellectual. Just as we walk into this room, we identify this space with this room and say, this room is too low, Ceiling is not too good.
Neeli should have made some ceiling or higher. Because we are affected by the conditioning, our perception affected by the conditioning. Same way Bhagavan said that Bhutana mi swopishan.
All beings are who they are because of my presence. This room exists because of room space. Just walls, floor and ceiling does not make the room.
The heart of this room is the space in the room. Without space, there is no room. Without self, there is no being.
So Bhagavan said, I am Isvar. I am the Lord of all beings. However, this universe I have put forth according to its own dharma.
Maya has its own Dharma. Sattvarajas and Tamas, those gunas and Dharmas are inherent in this universe. And when there is a decay of this Dharma, when those Dharmas decline, I as the Creator, will set it back.
I will participate actively in the creation. To set the creation back to as I design, time and again, we renovated my building. I designed something.
After a while it gets deteriorated. We just change carpet in my front room. Because when I designed in 2004, I had a perception what the room looks like.
Over time, the carpet got soiled. I have to the architect again and say, change the carpet. Now it looks the way I have thought in my mind before.
So Bhagawan said the same way, I come back again. Yadayadahi Dharma seglanir Bhavati. When the essential Dharma of this universe gets out of line, then I take active participation.
Just as I took active participation in creating this universe. Ill set the universe back to its Dharma. Paritra naya Sadhunam, Vina saya chaduskritam.
Whatever went out of Dharma, I will eliminate. And then whatever is in line with Dharma and protect it. So the Dharma principle will be restored.
And as I said, Dharma is a self regulating principle. As soon as you get out of your Dharma, you lost your existence. As soon as sugar loses its sweetness.
If you put sugar on frying pan and it becomes black, and now you put in your mouth, its not sweet. It lost its existence because its lost its Dharma. You wont call it sugar anymore.
So Bhagavan says, as soon as the Dharma gets out of line, the thing or being loses its existence. I destroy them by very fact that the Dharma is lost. So he said, therefore I come back again and again, every time.
So I assure you that my creation will always remain as I have designed. The will of Dharma makes it function. And then he said that every being still has to continue working.
All beings who are working, theyre working in my path alone. No matter what I am doing or you are doing, she is doing, he is doing -- everybody is functioning because of that consciousness in them. They are living beings.
Dead, Einstein cannot invent anything. As long as they are alive, they create. And whether I am going in the right direction or wrong direction in terms of my goals in life, as long as I take the support of my consciousness, it will allow me to go in the direction which I think is appropriate.
That is because of the equipment that I have. The equipment which I have will decide what direction I will take. My mind, my intellect, my body will determine what actions I am taking and what direction I will take.
Whatever my desires are. Therefore Kanksutta Karmanam Siddhi Ijanti IHA Devataha. Because we want success in this life.
We want success which is miserable success. Something which I can show people and say this is what I did in last 4 years, 5 years, 10 years. So what well do is something.
If say this is some pie in the sky type of a goal, I dont really pursue it. I want to pursue something which is I can show the result to the world. In this world getting results of your actions are easy and measurable and showable.
Therefore Bhagavan says Kangsadha Karmanam Siddhi Ijanti Ihadvattaha. Therefore we pursue those senses. Because I think I will get the results which I can enjoy.
The whole goal I have is to enjoy the fruits of my actions. I do not want to perform any action which I already know. There is no result for it.
If I know that I can keep working in this company and they wont ever promote me or will ever recognize my work. What is the normal advice? You better leave this company or find someplace else where you work and get results. So my fruits of actions are driving me.
Therefore people are pursuing different paths based on what they think will give them those results. My field is different than yours, and your field is different than hers. Next verse says Chaturvarnam Mayasrishtam Guna Karmaha Vibhagashah Kartaram Aphima Vidhi Kartaram Avyam.
This is not a social commentary on Indian caste system. This book was not written to have a commentary on whether a caste system is right or wrong. This book is a commentary about yourself.
Its a self development book. Gita was not written for you to learn and then teach other people. Gita was designed for you to learn yourself and make progress.
Now I dont know why I am putting these efforts in this field and not Going in. Why did I go to architecture school? I should have been smart enough to figure out that time that I should be there. Medical or maybe some business or Wall street type of commerce.
Nobody wanted to go in commerce. In my days, MBA wasnt even invented. I think it was there but nobody knew.
Nobody ever told me, Rajan, you can be mba. So only three options. I had you become a doctor.
Thats your first choice. Second was a chemical engineer, the second choice. And third, either electrical or civil engineering.
After that, no choice really. After that, BA, BA, BCom -- no value. Nobody told me that if you go to Commerce, Rajan, and become a Wall Street banker, youll be much better off than becoming an architect.
Why did you follow what you followed? Chaturvananyamaya Sristam Guna Karma Vibhaga Saha. Looking at the mental moods of people, you can say that the entire human race can be divided into four classifications. And Bhagwan says I created them.
Im taking full responsibility. Dont think that it was by accident that people are different from each other. Guna Karma Vibhaga Sah.
They need to be complementary. This society cannot function. If all want to be architects, there wont be any clients.
If I want to play a cop and robber game, somebody has to be the cop and somebody the robber, right? To play the game, I have to have both characters. To make this universe function, I need all the ingredients needed for this universe. To make the human race function, I need all types of people to make human society possible.

Krishna declares that the four-fold order of society was created by Him according to the natural distribution of qualities (gunas) and actions (karma). Yet immediately He adds: Though I am the author of this, know Me as the non-doer, immutable (tasya kartaram api mam viddhy akartaram avyayam). This is a profound teaching on the nature of the Self - actions take place, creation happens, yet the Self remains actionless. Just as space is not affected by good or bad architecture within it, the Self remains untainted by whatever occurs in body, mind, and intellect.
The key to freedom lies in understanding na mam karmani limpanti na me karma-phale spriha - actions do not taint Me, nor do I have desire for their fruits. Without desire for results, there can be no attachment, and without attachment, no bondage. This is not about the four castes of Indian society but about the four types of mental temperaments found in every society and within each individual. We each have qualities suited for different roles, and living according to our natural disposition (svadharma) is the path to harmony.
Today, reflect on your own natural temperament and tendencies. What type of work aligns with your inherent qualities? Are you forcing yourself into roles that contradict your nature, like trying to make a lecture hall into a concert hall? Practice viewing your actions as Krishna describes His own: you are the apparent author, yet at your core, you remain the actionless witness. When you catch yourself anxious about results, remember that the sufferer and enjoyer is only the ego - the body, mind, and intellect. The Self within you, like space within a room, remains forever free and unchanged.
